t: The Mississippian culture was a way of life shared from about 800 to 1600 by many Native American peoples of the Mississippi valley and the South-East, built on maize farming and hereditary chiefs.
Its towns centred on earthen platform mounds and plazas, from Cahokia, the largest, to Moundville in Alabama, Etowah in Georgia and Spiro in Oklahoma.
Spanish expeditions from 1539 met its last great chiefdoms; after epidemics, wars and slave raids their peoples regrouped as the Creek, Choctaw, Chickasaw and other nations.
dyk: Chunkey, a game in which players threw poles after a rolling stone disc, spread from the Cahokia region with Mississippian ways; Creek, Choctaw and Chickasaw men still played it in the 18th century, and the Cherokee have revived it.
ev: Emergent Mississippian villages in the central Mississippi valley come to depend on maize
Cahokia is rebuilt around a great plaza and becomes the largest town north of Mexico
Mississippian ways spread across the South-East; Moundville becomes a regional capital
Cahokia, long in decline, is largely abandoned
Towns around the meeting of the Ohio and Mississippi are abandoned, leaving a “Vacant Quarter”
Hernando de Soto’s expedition marches through the Mississippian chiefdoms
De Soto’s army burns the town of Mabila after an ambush; thousands of its people die
Juan Pardo’s expeditions build forts at Joara and other towns, destroyed by their people by 1568

f.homeland: The Mississippi valley and its tributaries and the south-eastern United States, from Wisconsin to the Gulf of Mexico and from eastern Oklahoma to Georgia, the Carolinas and Florida
f.period: c. 800–1600 CE: Emergent Mississippian villages from about 800; Cahokia’s rise about 1050; regional centres such as Moundville and Etowah from the 12th to the 16th centuries; the last chiefdoms met by Spanish expeditions in 1539–1568
f.known: Towns of earthen platform mounds around plazas, Monks Mound at Cahokia the largest; maize farming; chiefdoms ruled by hereditary elites; shell-tempered pottery; the copper, shell and stone art of the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex
f.sources: Excavations at Cahokia, Moundville, Etowah, Spiro, Lake Jackson and hundreds of other sites; the chronicles of Hernando de Soto’s expedition by the Gentleman of Elvas, Rodrigo Rangel, Luys Hernández de Biedma and Garcilaso de la Vega; the records of Juan Pardo’s expeditions; French accounts of the Natchez; the traditions of descendant nations
